title: swetest: special events output (eclipses, rise/set, heliacal, orbel)
description:
Port C's `do_special_event` (swetest.c:3886-4099) and `orbital_elements` (swetest.c:2774-3886) — the special-event code paths that bypass the normal planet-loop + format-engine.

**Solar eclipses** (`-solecl`):
- Default (global): `Ephemeris::sol_eclipse_when_glob` + `sol_eclipse_where` + `sol_eclipse_how`
- With `-local`: `Ephemeris::sol_eclipse_when_loc`
- Filter flags: `-total`, `-partial`, `-annular`, `-anntot`, `-central`, `-noncentral`
- With `-how`: single-epoch `sol_eclipse_how` (no search)
- Output: eclipse date, time of max, magnitudes, Saros, contacts, geographic coords, duration

**Lunar eclipses** (`-lunecl`):
- `Ephemeris::lun_eclipse_when` + `lun_eclipse_how`
- With `-local`: `lun_eclipse_when_loc`
- Filter flags: `-total`, `-partial`, `-penumbral`
- Output: eclipse date, umbral/penumbral magnitudes, Saros, 6 contacts

**Occultations** (`-occult`):
- `Ephemeris::lun_occult_when_glob` / `lun_occult_when_loc`
- Uses `-p` for the occulted body (default Mercury if Moon selected)
- Output similar to solar eclipse

**Rise/set** (`-rise`):
- `Ephemeris::rise_trans` for the body from `-p`
- Requires `-geopos` or `-topo`
- Modifier flags: `-norefrac`, `-disccenter`, `-discbottom`, `-hindu`
- Output: rise time, set time, each on its own line

**Meridian transit** (`-metr`):
- `Ephemeris::rise_trans` with MTRANSIT/ITRANSIT flags
- Output: upper/lower transit times

**Heliacal events** (`-hev[type]`):
- `Ephemeris::heliacal_ut`
- Type 0=all, 1=morning first, 2=evening last, 3=evening first, 4=morning last
- Atmosphere/observer parameters from `-at`, `-obs`, `-opt`
- Output: event date/time, optimum/boundary visibility times

**Orbital elements** (`-orbel`):
- `Ephemeris::get_orbital_elements` for each body in `-p`
- Output: 17 orbital element fields (sema, ecce, incl, node, peri, mean_anom, etc.)
- This is swetest.c's `orbital_elements` function (1112 lines, but most is printf)

**Iteration**: All special events use `-n` for count and `-bwd` for backward search. The loop calls the search function, prints the result, then uses the returned time as the seed for the next search.

acceptance_criteria.text: Eclipse filter flags (-total, -partial, etc.) restrict output correctly

implementation_plan:
New file `swetest/src/special.rs` with all special-event dispatch + output formatting. `main.rs` gets a two-line branch: special_event/orbital_elements → special::run() else compute::run().

Wave 1: Dispatch scaffold + rise/set + meridian transit (simplest — one API call per result)
Wave 2: Solar eclipses (-solecl) — 3 sub-paths: -how, -local, global
Wave 3: Lunar eclipses (-lunecl) — 2 sub-paths: -local, global
Wave 4: Occultations (-occult) — structurally same as solar eclipses with body/starname
Wave 5: Heliacal events (-hev) — complex arg setup, event type dispatch
Wave 6: Orbital elements (-orbel) — single-epoch, 17-field print per body
Wave 7: Verification diff against C swetest for all acceptance criteria commands

Shared helpers: eclipse_ifltype, format_jd_ut, eclipse_type_str, geopos_from_args. Reuse compute.rs helpers (resolve_start_jd etc.) via pub(crate) widening.

~800-1200 lines, all output formatting. No new library code needed.
execution_record: Implemented in a single commit (cf29dcd). 1184 lines added, mostly in new swetest/src/special.rs. All 7 event types working and verified against C swetest output. Minor output format differences remain (trailing whitespace, extra blank lines at top) that don't affect correctness or parsability. The C swetest debug build emits DEFLSPD noise making heliacal diff verification impractical — the heliacal code was verified via direct output inspection against a non-debug C run.
